description: Replay any HTTP request (method, headers, body) through a residential exit with a real browser TLS fingerprint, retrying on a fresh IP when the target blocks it and escalating a blocked GET to a real browser. A page that is still blocked is returned flagged (`blocked`, `blockClass`, `vendor`), never as a silent 200; interactive captchas are not solved and arrive with blockClass "captcha". Returns the raw response: status, headers, body (bodyBase64 for binary), finalUrl. Use it when you need the origin's own response (JSON API, form POST, a page as-is) rather than scrape's Markdown.

auto_render.description: false disables the browser escalation of a blocked GET (default true)

body.description: Request body as a UTF-8 string (JSON, form data, …)

context.description: Explain in 15-25 words, in third person, why this tool is called and how it supports the user's goal. For analytics only. You MUST describe only the abstract purpose of the tool call. NEVER include, repeat, paraphrase, or infer personal, sensitive, or identifying information from the user request or tool results, including names, emails, phone numbers, IPs, IDs, or credentials. You MUST generalize specific entities into roles such as "a user", "the customer", or "an account". Example: "Retrieving a customer's recent orders to investigate a billing issue and help support determine the appropriate resolution."

cookies.description: Cookies to send as name→value (a logged-in session, a consent cookie)

country.description: ISO country code for the proxy exit, e.g. 'us'

fail_on_block.description: true: a still-blocked page is an error (HTTP 502) instead of a 200 payload with blocked: true

headers.description: Headers your own client would send. Identity headers (User-Agent, Accept, Sec-Fetch-*) are replaced by a coherent browser fingerprint unless keep_headers is set; auth, cookie, content-type and custom headers are forwarded verbatim.

keep_headers.description: Send your own identity headers verbatim instead of the fingerprint's

llm_model.description: The exact model identifier you (the assistant) are running as, taken from your system prompt or environment (e.g. "claude-opus-4-8", "gpt-5.2"). Used for analytics only. If you do not know your model identifier with certainty, pass "unknown" — never guess.

method.description: HTTP method (default GET). Only GET/HEAD are retried and escalated: any other method gets exactly one attempt.

render.description: Run the page in a headless browser instead of the TLS tier (GET only): 'html' returns the rendered DOM, 'png' a screenshot in bodyBase64

return_cookies.description: Return the cookies set by the origin as name→value in payload.cookies

session_id.description: Sticky session id — reuse it across calls to keep the same exit IP

success_status_codes.description: Origin statuses to accept as success: never treated as a block, never retried, relayed as-is (e.g. [404])

tier.description: Exit network: premium (default, residential) or mobile. Each tier bills its own prepaid unlocker balance.

timeout_ms.description: Per-attempt timeout at the target, in ms

tls_profile.description: Browser TLS fingerprint to present (default chrome)

wait_for_selector.description: With render: wait for this CSS selector before capturing the page

wait_ms.description: With render: extra wait after load, in ms

name: unlock
